item.title: Brownian motion in Riemannian manifolds
item.description: Random walks are the quintessential building blocks of stochastic processes. From Einstein’s explanation of Brownian motion to the discrete-time models underpinning modern option pricing, the premise is deceptively simple: at each step, take an independent, identically distributed (IID) jump in a random direction. In Euclidean space \(\mathbb{R}^n\), this is trivial, as all position vectors share the same global tangent space. However, when the state space is a curved manifold—say, the space of covariance matrices, the configuration space of a rigid body, or the parameter space of an interest rate curve—the very notion of “stepping in the same direction” breaks down. To extend the random walk to a curved geometry, we must first understand how to “go straight” on a manifold. This is precisely the role of a Riemannian metric and its associated geodesics.
